transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-02
Time: 14:00 - 14:52 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Evan Morales (Redwood SE), Samantha Reed (Cedarline - Head of ML), Marco Diaz (Cedarline - Cloud Architect), Priya Singh (Cedarline - CTO)

Summary:
Redwood did a Console walkthrough focused on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown. Customer asked about dedicated vs hosted cost tradeoffs, data residency, and SLA. Agreed to share pricing, security docs, and schedule a POC perf run.

Topics: per-route dashboards, tail latency, token distribution, batching and caching impact on cost, dedicated/reserved capacity, VPC/private deployment, SOC2, canary rollouts, quality regressions monitoring.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro — I'm Jordan, AE for Redwood, and Evan's our SE who will drive the console walkthrough. How's everyone doing?
[00:10] Samantha (Cedarline): Hi Jordan, good thanks. Busy quarter but excited to see this.
[00:15] Priya (Cedarline): Hey all. We'll be watching mainly for cost visibility and how rollout controls work.
[00:22] Jordan: Great. Evan, take it away.
[00:25] Evan (Redwood SE): Sure. I'll share my screen — let me know if you can't see. So this is the Console dashboard. Top-left we have an overview: total calls, tokens ingested, cost by day. You can filter by route, model, and environment.
[00:40] Evan: Quick note — some of the names in the console are autopopulated, so if you see, like, 'read wood dedicated' that's just my bad naming in the demo, ignore that 
[00:48] Marco (Cedarline): (laughs) noted.
[00:50] Evan: First pane — per-route traffic. Shows QPS, p50/p95/p99 latency, and cost-per-1000-requests and cost-per-1M-tokens. You can click a route to expand and see model mapping, batching profile, and whether KV cache is enabled. Sorry, I say KV cache but sometimes the transcription on my slides says KV cash — classic.
[01:15] Samantha: Can you show the route-level cost breakdown? That's what our finance team will want.
[01:20] Evan: Yep. Here we have a per-route cost table — split by model, quantization profile, and infra tier (hosted vs dedicated). You can toggle time window and group by model version. For example, Route 'inbox-summarize' is 42% of token volume but only 28% of cost due to prefix caching and batching.
[01:40] Priya: How do you compute cost? Is it purely tokens * model price? What about infra amortization for Dedicated?
[01:48] Jordan: Good question. We show both a usage-based cost (tokens * model unit price) and an effective unit cost that includes amortized reserved capacity for Dedicated. The console lets you view both side-by-side so you can see the delta.
[02:03] Marco: For Dedicated, do we get a per-GPU utilization metric in the console? We need to understand tail scenarios.
[02:09] Evan: Yes — infra tab shows GPU pools, utilization, avg batch size, and cold-starts. Tail latency percentiles come from the serving logs; we overlay the P99 and P99.9 with the SLA target.
[02:22] Samantha: Our main worry is unpredictable cost from spiky traffic. Can Redwood throttle or route to cheaper models automatically?
[02:29] Evan: We have smart routing policies. You can set policy rules like prefer-lower-cost up to X ms, or fallback-models for overflow. There's an auto-burst setting that will use hosted spare capacity for short spikes. We can demo that in the POC.
[02:45] Priya: Any guardrails for quality when routing to cheaper models? We need regression alerts.
[02:51] Evan: Absolutely. The Console has quality monitoring: you can attach prompt sets and expected outputs as monitors. When model outputs drift or regression score drops, you get alerts and automatic rollback options on the rollout page.
[03:05] Jordan: We're going to put a link to the quality monitoring doc in the follow-up.
[03:09] Samantha: Great. Can you share the SOC2 and data residency stuff?
[03:13] Evan: Yes — we'll send SOC2 and our security whitepaper. For Private/VPC deployments, customers keep the control plane in their VPC; logs and data residency options are configurable. Note: on-prem add-on is possible if needed.
[03:26] Marco: For VPC, what's the network egress pattern? We have strict firewall rules.
[03:31] Evan: We provide a static IP list for egress and can do peering. We'll include a VPC deployment checklist in the packet.
[03:39] Priya: Pricing question — what's the delta between hosted and dedicated? Our ops team likes predictability.
[03:45] Jordan: Hosted is usage-based — flexible but variable. Dedicated uses reserved GPU capacity; per-token cost goes down but you pay commit. The Console sim has a slider that shows break-even points given your QPS and token mix.
[03:58] Evan: (shows slider) For example at 120 QPS sustained, Dedicated reduces effective per-token cost by ~35% for a 7B quantized model, given our current pricing. We'll put exact numbers in the spreadsheet.
[04:12] Samantha: Can you export per-route cost to CSV? Our finance wants the raw numbers.
[04:16] Evan: Yes — export CSV or connect to your BI via our API. There's also an endpoint to pull per-route metrics programmatically.
[04:24] Marco: About batching — can we configure max latency vs batch size? We care about 95th latency more than median.
[04:30] Evan: You can set per-route latency SLOs and batching curves. The runtime will attempt to meet the SLO by capping batch size for latency-sensitive routes, and allow larger batches on background routes to save cost.
[04:44] Samantha: Any gotchas with prefix caching? Our summaries reuse similar prefixes.
[04:49] Evan: Prefix/KV caching works well for repeat prefixes; the console shows cache hit rates per route. Note that privacy-sensitive data shouldn't be cached unless you opt-in; we have per-route cache control flags.
[04:59] Priya: Can we see a demo of a canary rollout?
[05:02] Evan: Sure — opening the Rollouts tab. Here you define a new model version, set an initial 5% traffic, configure canary metrics (latency, quality score, error rate), and automatic promotion or rollback rules.
[05:16] Evan: (narration) If the P95 increases beyond 20% or quality drops below threshold, the canary will automatically roll back. You can also set manual approval.
[05:28] Marco: How do we instrument custom metrics? We have internal quality checks.
[05:33] Evan: You can push custom metrics via our tracing API; they show up in the per-route dashboard and can be used for rollout decisions.
[05:40] Samantha: About long-term cost monitoring — do you support budgets/alerts?
[05:44] Evan: Yes, budget alerts, forecasted monthly spend, and anomaly detection for sudden usage spikes. The Console will email and post to Slack integrations.
[05:54] Priya: Ok, I'm sold on the visibility. A couple red flags for our legal team: retention of logs and auditability.
[06:01] Jordan: Audit logs are available and retention is configurable. For Private customers we can configure retention to meet compliance needs. We'll include the audit log spec in the pack.
[06:12] Samantha: For the POC, our success criteria: 1) demonstrate 30% cost reduction vs our current self-hosted baseline with similar quality, 2) confirm P99 latency under 250ms for our interactive route, 3) automatic rollback on quality regressions.
[06:27] Jordan: Noted. We'll base the POC scope on those.
[06:30] Evan: Quick note on the perf bench: we'll need a representative traffic CSV and sample prompts. Marco?
[06:36] Marco: I'll export our traffic profile and share. Expect it by Monday.
[06:40] Evan: Great. I'll also attach our benchmark spreadsheet and a quickstart for running the POC. Link in chat: https://redwood.dev/console-walkthrough and benchmark sheet: https://drive.google.com/cedarline-bench
[06:54] Samantha: Can you show how errors are surfaced in the console?
[06:57] Evan: Errors tab shows error type, rate, and trace links. We store a sample of outputs (configurable) for debugging. You can search by request id.
[07:08] Priya: Are request IDs accessible to our SRE?
[07:10] Evan: Yes — request IDs are returned in the response and in logs. For private deployments they remain inside your VPC if you choose.
[07:18] (Demo continues, Evan toggles filters and simulates a traffic spike)
[07:44] Jordan: We should summarize next steps. I'll send pricing, Evan will send security docs and the VPC checklist, Marco will share traffic CSV and Samantha will finalize POC success criteria.
[07:57] Priya: Sounds good. Anything else?
[08:00] Samantha: One last question — does Redwood support token-level cost attribution for multi-turn chats? We have a chat summarizer that spawns follow-ups.
[08:09] Evan: We attribute tokens to the initiating route and you can see per-turn token breakdown in the session view. Multi-turn chains are assigned to the parent route so finance can attribute cost cleanly.
[08:22] Marco: Good. We'll aim to have legal review shortly after we get SOC2.
[08:27] Jordan: Perfect — thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the materials and a proposed POC calendar.
[08:31] End of recording.
